From today's featured article
Exterior of Eunos MRT station
Eunos MRT station is a Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station on the East–West Line (EWL) in Geylang, Singapore. Operated by SMRT Trains, the station is connected to the Eunos Bus Interchange and provides access to nearby landmarks such as the Masjid Darul Aman and the Mangala Vihara Buddhist Temple. Eunos appeared in plans for the initial MRT system in May1982, and construction of the station began in January 1986 under a joint venture between Oh Teck Thye and Okumura Corporation. Oh Teck Thye was placed under receivership in December1986, terminating the joint venture, with Okumura continuing the project alone. Eunos, along with nine other stations from Marina Bay to Tanah Merah, opened on 4November 1989. Platform screen doors were installed at Eunos in 2011. Unlike adjacent EWL elevated stations, which have domed roofs, Eunos has a traditional Malay roof. The station also has two murals as part of SMRT's heritage-themed Comic Connect public art display. (Fullarticle...)

Did you know...
Artist's conception of Pioneer 10
... that the radioisotope thermoelectric generators on the Pioneer 10(conception pictured) spacecraft were designed to last for at least two years, but continued operating for over thirty?
... that a "Gong Show" tryout led to football running back Vince Thompson becoming an NFL leader?
... that, after literary agents described Your Name Here as difficult to follow, co-author Helen DeWitt responded by adding more material?
... that Antonio Peña y Goñi has been described as the founder of modern music criticism in Spain?
... that the Canadian Space Agency developed Canasnack, an oatmeal cookie made solely out of Canadian ingredients?
... that Christopher H. Bidmead became the script editor for Doctor Who after writing a "fan letter"?
... that Faker celebrated winning the 2015 League of Legends World Championship by eating a raw broccoli stalk on stage?
... that Rewind became the first Philippine film to gross 900million pesos at the worldwide box office?
... that there are generally no age restrictions for lotteries in Japan?
